title: Identity, Sameness, Replay and History
results: Identity must name the entity kind, scope and lifetime being tracked.
Identity persists across selected state changes and is distinct from equality of all state/content/properties.
Token identity, content equality, structural equality, semantic equivalence and observational equivalence are distinct relations.
Content-addressed identity is powerful for immutable objects but is not a universal mutable-resource identity model.
Identifier values such as UUID/hash/name/locator do not by themselves define semantic identity contracts.
Request identity is best represented by a receiver-scoped continuity key plus semantic fingerprint.
Current clientRequestId and request/proposal digest correctly occupy those two different roles.
Replay preserves historical request interpretation across current world/source/policy/provider drift.
Current jobId and operationDigest are complementary: durable entity handle and committed operation fingerprint.
Attempt identity is one physical realization generation below Operation identity.
Launch token is an integrity/lineage binding between Attempt and Operation rather than either entity's identity.
External Effect, resource and receipt identities are distinct from Runtime Operation/Attempt identities.
Identity lifetime and tombstones matter for late requests, deletion/recreation and idempotency safety.
Replay, Retry, ReExecution, ReObservation and Reconciliation are distinct operations over identity/history.
Deterministic reproduction or equal output does not make execution occurrences historically identical.
History is multi-projection rather than one universal event log.
Superseding evidence/state correction should preserve prior historical claims/evidence.
Current Ordivon layered identity stack receives foundation-level support; one universal ID would erase necessary distinctions.

nextRound.title: Time, Ordering, Concurrency and Causality
nextRound.entryQuestion: Given distinct entities and histories, which temporal/logical/causal/serialization relations order their events and behaviors, and which apparent orders are merely observations?

notes: RF4 explains layered Runtime identity/replay semantics but does not authorize identifier replacement, new retry behavior, multi-Attempt execution or Registry-history rewriting.
